title: Mismanagement of the army chief medical officer (Stettbacher) affair
description: While head of the DDPS, Parmelin suspended the army's chief medical officer Andreas Stettbacher in December 2016 over suspected expense irregularities, and a criminal complaint was filed. An administrative investigation cleared Stettbacher, who was reinstated in October 2017 and the complaint withdrawn. The National Council's Control Committee (GPC) criticised Parmelin for the way he had handled the procedure.
status: concluded; subject reinstated and cleared, Parmelin criticised by parliamentary oversight body
key_facts: Stettbacher suspended in December 2016; criminal complaint filed with the Federal Prosecutor's Office
Administrative investigation found no labour-law or disciplinary fault; allegations prescribed or unconfirmed
Stettbacher reinstated on 1 October 2017 and the criminal complaint withdrawn
Parliamentary Control Committee faulted Parmelin's handling of the case

title: Alleged conflict of interest on taxation of agricultural land
description: As a National Councillor, Parmelin advocated tax relief on gains from the sale of building-zone agricultural land. Media reported that his family (his brother in Bursins) held such land, raising questions about whether he should have declared a personal interest before intervening in the debate.
status: reported by media; no formal sanction
key_facts: Parmelin supported exempting/limiting tax on capital gains from sales of building-zone agricultural land
Press reported family-held land in Bursins that could benefit from the relief
Questions raised over whether he should have flagged a personal interest in the parliamentary debate

title: Dispute over the F-35 fighter jet fixed price
description: Switzerland stated it had agreed a firm price of just over 6 billion francs for 36 F-35A jets in 2022. In June 2025 Swiss public broadcaster SRF reported the bill could rise by 1.3-1.5 billion francs, with the United States describing the fixed price as a 'misunderstanding'. The National Council's Control Committee opened an inquiry into the information the Federal Council gave to Parliament and the public; the government later signalled fewer jets could be bought. Parmelin negotiated the original procurement as DDPS head; the EAER/economic department and the current DDPS are also involved.
key_facts: 2022 agreement cited a firm price of just over CHF 6 billion for 36 F-35A jets
June 2025 SRF report: potential cost increase of CHF 1.3-1.5 billion
US side characterised the fixed price as a 'misunderstanding'
National Council Control Committee opened an inquiry; government considered reducing the number of jets purchased
